title: Record, Exclude, Extract, and NonNullable
hook: Record<K, V> builds string-keyed object types; Exclude and Extract filter union members; NonNullable strips null and undefined — the set-theory toolkit for composing precise types.

blocks.text: **Record<K, V>** = `{ [P in K]: V }` — object with keys `K` and values `V`. `Record<string, T>` is the typed index signature. **Exclude<U, X>** removes union members assignable to `X`: `Exclude<'a'|'b'|'c', 'a'>` → `'b'|'c'`. **Extract<U, X>** keeps members assignable to `X`. **NonNullable<T>** = `Exclude<T, null | undefined>`. These are **conditional type** shortcuts built into lib.d.ts.

entries.plainDefinition: Mapped type building object with keys K and uniform value type V.
Union U without members assignable to X.
Union members of U assignable to X.
Removes null and undefined from T.

blocks.text: Route tables: `Record<HttpMethod, RouteHandler>`. Theme tokens: `Record<ThemeKey, string>`. Omit implementation uses `Exclude<keyof T, K>`. Filtering event unions: `Extract<Action, { type: 'user/*' }>`. After optional chaining, `NonNullable<T>` asserts presence. C# uses `where T : notnull` and pattern matching — TS uses union algebra. Senior interviews combine Record + keyof for lookup tables and Exclude for branded type stripping.

blocks.title: Record keys
blocks.body: Record<string, V> allows any string key — for finite keys use union: Record<'a'|'b', V>.

blocks.title: Record<string, T> typos
blocks.body: Use union keys for finite sets — catches missing and misspelled keys.

blocks.title: Exclude on non-unions
blocks.body: Exclude distributes — on non-union behaves as filter against assignability.

blocks.text: Record is implemented as mapped type — customize with `Record<K, V | undefined>` for partial maps. Exclude powers Omit, Diff, and Never keys. Extract with conditional types filters discriminated union members by kind. `as const` object keys become union for Record keys. Combine: `Record<Exclude<keyof T, 'id'>, T[keyof T]>` for advanced patterns.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot explain Omit uses Exclude. Record vs index signature confusion. NonNullable vs optional (?).

interviewTakeaways: Record<K,V> = mapped type { [P in K]: V }.
Exclude removes union members; Extract keeps them; NonNullable strips null|undefined.
60s: Record for lookup tables with finite key unions. Exclude/Extract are union set ops. NonNullable after filter. Prefer Record<Union,V> over Record<string,V> for safety.
Follow-up: implement Exclude with conditional types, Record + satisfies.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "Record is runtime Map" — type-level object shape.
Record<string, T> when keys are finite union.
Strong: "Record maps keys to values. Exclude/Extract filter unions. Omit built on Exclude."

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS objects have string/symbol keys at runtime — Record types the expected key set at compile time.
C# Dictionary<K,V> is runtime; Record<K,V> is compile-time shape — JSON deserializes to plain object not Record type.
